title: Arctic climate change in 21st century CMIP5 simulations with EC-Earth
problem: Existing climate models exhibit significant spread and biases, like overestimating sea ice extent and underestimating reduction trends, creating uncertainty in projections of accelerated 21st-century Arctic climate change under different emission scenarios.
method: This paper analyzes 21st-century Arctic climate change using an ensemble of future projection simulations performed with the global coupled climate model EC-Earth under various Representative Concentration Pathway (RCP) scenarios and comparing them to twentieth-century data.
task: The task is to analyze 21st-century Arctic climate change using an ensemble of future projection simulations from the EC-Earth global climate model based on different CMIP5 emission scenarios.
innovation: This paper analyzes an ensemble of future Arctic climate projections using the EC-Earth model, detailing dramatic 21st-century changes including amplified warming, a rapid loss of summer sea ice by 2060 under high emissions, and significant shifts in ocean and atmospheric heat transport.

Here, we used the model version 2.3.
